title: Source catalog
description: The sources a skill, instruction or document draws its claims from. The same shape serves the root sources.json and every shard in sources.d.

preamble.description: Prose that introduces the catalog and belongs to no single source.

notes.description: Prose sections that describe how the catalog is kept and belong to no single source.

kind.description: How an audit reads the source: a git checkout, an http document, a file on disk, a web page, a repository path, or repository-original material with no address.

anchor.description: The heading slug, line range or fragment of the source that backs the claim.

evidence.description: A quotation or observation from the source at the anchor.

watch.description: A path of a checkout whose changes since the pinned commit affect the files that draw on it.

after.description: The id of the source this section follows. A section without it comes before the first source.

citation.description: How the source is cited when that differs from the heading, such as the title of a book.

urls.description: The documents that make up the source, in the order their digest is taken.

urlNotes.description: The lines of a URL list that say more than a bare URL, verbatim, so the wording survives next to the fetch list.

ref.description: The git commit, tag or branch that pins a git source.

checkout.description: The local clone of the upstream repository, relative to the directory of the catalog.

version.description: The release of the upstream the feeds were written against.

commit.description: The upstream commit the feeds were written against.

contentSha256.description: The digest of the fetched documents, in the order of urls or of the file that path names.

outputSha256.description: The digest of the output of the commands that were run to read a program-defined source.

provenance.description: How the source was obtained when it has no address of its own.

feeds.description: The files that draw on this source, relative to the directory of the catalog.

coversAllReferences.description: True when every reference file of the catalog draws on this source.

usage.description: How the feeds use the source, one statement for each use.

remarks.description: Prose about the source that fits no other field.
